data.title: Add docker-compose with Django, Postgres, and RabbitMQ services

data.body:
Reviewed commit 006d05b cold (plan file + git diff), then verified behavior against every acceptance criterion on a live engine.

WHAT I REVIEWED
- .lattice/plans/task_01KYQFPKMR7S32QWYA4KJXCNV0.md vs the actual diff: docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile, requirements.txt, .env.example, .dockerignore.
- Ran: docker compose config; docker compose build web; docker compose up -d db rabbitmq; a persistence probe across docker compose down/up; and a docker compose run against web exercising env plumbing and network reachability.

VERIFIED (all 5 acceptance criteria met)
1. docker compose config parses clean; all interpolations resolve.
2. db and rabbitmq both reach 'healthy'. pg_isready and rabbitmq-diagnostics -q check_running both pass.
3. web runs 'python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000' and gates on service_healthy for both deps — compose logged 'db Healthy'/'rabbitmq Healthy' before creating the web container.
4. Persistence confirmed empirically: created a table + row in postgres, ran docker compose down (no -v), brought db back up, row still there. Named volumes postgres_data/rabbitmq_data, no anonymous mounts.
5. No secrets in the diff. .env.example is placeholders only; the local .env is untracked.
Also confirmed inside the built image: Python 3.14.6, Django 6.0.7, psycopg 3.3.4, celery 5.6.3 all import; runs as uid 1000 (app), not root. web connected to postgres via POSTGRES_HOST=db/POSTGRES_PORT=5432 (correctly hardcoded to the container port rather than the host-override var — good catch by the implementer) and opened a TCP session to rabbitmq:5672. CELERY_BROKER_URL resolves to amqp://guest:guest@rabbitmq:5672// (vhost '/', correct).

FIXED INLINE (commit abaf772)
- .gitignore was untracked. It was the only thing keeping the local .env — which contains a generated DJANGO_SECRET_KEY — out of git, and a fresh clone would have had no such protection. Committed it and extended it with the usual Python/Django artifacts (__pycache__, *.py[cod], .venv, *.sqlite3, staticfiles, tool caches, .DS_Store). Criterion 5 passed as-is, but the safeguard behind it was not actually in the repo.

NON-BLOCKING NOTES FOR THE NEXT AGENT
- Plan deviations, all defensible and disclosed in the commit message: python:3.14-slim (plan said 3.12), rabbitmq:4-management (plan said 3-management-alpine; upstream discontinued alpine tags), healthcheck check_running (plan said check_port_connectivity). Verified working. check_port_connectivity is marginally stronger as a readiness signal since check_running reports the app is up without asserting the 5672 listener is accepting — small race window for web startup, not worth a rework on its own.
- Portability: bind-mounting .:/app under USER app (uid 1000) works on Docker Desktop for macOS (verified a write into /app), but on a Linux host whose developer uid != 1000 in-container writes to /app will be denied. That matters immediately, because the next step is scaffolding the project from inside the container (django-admin startproject / makemigrations). A UID build arg is the usual mitigation.
- .dockerignore excludes *.md, so README.md will not be in the image. Harmless in dev (bind mount restores it); flagging only so it isn't a surprise later.
- celery is in requirements and the broker URL is plumbed, but there is no worker service — out of scope per the plan, noting so it is not forgotten.
- PROMPT.md requires a README.md with setup steps; that deliverable belongs to the app-scaffolding work, not this task. (A README.md appeared untracked in the worktree during this review — apparently a sibling agent's in-flight work. Left untouched per shared-worktree discipline.)
- Insecure defaults (DJANGO_DEBUG=1, guest/guest, placeholder secret key) are appropriate here and nothing in the diff presents this stack as production-ready.

VERDICT: PASS (after the inline .gitignore fix described above).
